title: Opinionated SDK examples & ergonomic patterns: Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP server, CLI
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create an opinionated, lightweight examples repository and cookbook that showcases SDK ergonomics and recommended patterns across TypeScript (Next.js), Python (FastAPI), Go (HTTP server), and CLI tools. Goals: 1) provide copy-paste starters that demonstrate streaming, retry/backoff, cancellation, and token-cost-aware batching; 2) surface best practices for SDK usage (sync vs async, streaming APIs, error classification); 3) ship tests and CI so examples remain runnable; 4) include short runnable cookbook snippets for common patterns (exponential backoff in Python, async iterator streaming in TypeScript, context cancellation & retries in Go, local dev flow for CLI). Deliverables: - repo skeleton with four top-level examples: nextjs-app, fastapi-stream, go-server, cli-demo - README for each example with setup, env vars, sample prompts and expected outputs - small utility modules showing recommended retry/backoff, request decorators/middleware, and lightweight wrappers for streaming consumption - unit + integration tests (playback fixtures) and GitHub Actions to run smoke tests on PRs - one-page guide summarizing ergonomics tradeoffs (performance vs simplicity) and migration notes from older SDK versions Acceptance criteria: - each example runs locally with documented steps on macOS/Linux - streaming examples demonstrate partial-response rendering (Next.js/CLI) and server-sent style streaming for FastAPI/Go - retry strategy utilities are implemented in each language and covered by tests - PR with implementation passes review and includes links to docs PR and demo screencast Notes on ergonomics and design decisions: - Streaming: TypeScript will expose an async iterator of events and a convenience .stream() helper that integrates with React Suspense/SSR patterns in Next.js examples. Python will use async generators and a sync wrapper for Flask/Blocking server examples. Go will stream via http.Flusher with clear examples of chunk framing and a small helper that converts SDK token chunks to JSON events. - Retries: Provide two-level retry helpers: transient-retry (idempotent safe retries with jittered exponential backoff) and once-only fast-fail for non-idempotent calls. Retry classification is pluggable via error codes and response shapes. - Cancellation: All examples will demonstrate context/cancellation: AbortController in TypeScript, asyncio.CancelledError patterns in Python, context.Context in Go. - Security: example.env files will show KMS/HSM integrations as comments and not contain secrets. - Cost considerations: demonstrate prefix caching and optional batching harness in the Go/TypeScript examples with simple metrics outputs.
